units.text: EXT. SALT FLAT - DAY
An infinite white plain.
Heat shimmers off the crust.
The horizon is a thin, wavering line.
A dead jeep sits tilted on a collapsed tire, doors open.
A rusted antenna leans from its roof.
Sky the color of old bone.
BRONWYN ACHEBE-TULLY (40s, sun-cracked lips, cotton scarf wrapped around her head, a backpack with its straps cut) sits in the jeep's shade, knees to her chest.
She holds a battered voice recorder.
A canteen hangs empty from the mirror.
She turns the recorder on.
A red light blinks.
Day four. Or five. I've lost the count.
units.name: BRONWYN

units.text: She lays her head against the door.
Water's gone. Last of the crackers went yesterday. The tire is flat and the spare is flatter. The radio died on day two.
units.name: BRONWYN

units.text: She lifts the antenna in her hand and lets it drop.
They told me this place has no sound. They were wrong. It ticks. Like a clock somewhere underground.
units.name: BRONWYN

units.text: She wipes salt from her eyes.
If anyone finds this, tell my sister the key is under the geranium. The one with the red pot. She'll know.
units.name: BRONWYN

units.text: She stops.
Presses stop.
Rewinds.
The tape whirs.
...Day four. Or five. I've lost the count.
units.name: BRONWYN

units.text: She listens to her own voice for a time.
She smiles a little.
She presses stop again, then record.
I'm not afraid. That's the odd thing. I thought I'd be afraid.
units.name: BRONWYN

units.text: She watches the horizon.
A shape wavers there, a mirage, a pillar of shimmer.
There's something out there. A person, maybe. Or the heat. It's walking.
units.name: BRONWYN

units.text: She stands, unsteady, one hand on the roof.
I'll go meet it. If that's all right.
units.name: BRONWYN

units.text: She sets the recorder on the jeep's hood, still running, and starts across the white plain.
...if that's all right.
units.name: BRONWYN

units.text: The light blinks.
The wind scours the plain.
Her footprints are the only mark.
